name: Macaroni and Cheese
lede: Macaroni and Cheese is a warm, pale orange named for the baked pasta dish, recorded by both Wikipedia and the 2010 xkcd color survey as the same hue.

sections.title: Named for a dish, not a crayon
sections.body:
The color library cites both Wikipedia and the xkcd survey for this exact name and hex, #FFBD88, with the xkcd community separately logging an alternate, more saturated version at #EFB435 under the same name [1][2]. Unlike Crayola's similarly food-named crayons, which the company documents with release years and naming contests, no source here gives a date or an author for when this orange was first called Macaroni and Cheese, so its coining is undocumented [1][2].

The 1955 ISCC-NBS system's closest block is plainly "light orange," only 2.1 units away[2]. In Munsell terms it sits at 5.4YR 8.1/6.8, and it falls close to [[apricot]], [[peach]] and [[orange]] in the library, all within a narrow range [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our 23,781-painting archive, a color within six units of Macaroni and Cheese covers at least one per cent of the canvas in 103 paintings, as photographed, more common than half the named colors tracked [3]. It most often plays an accent, in 52 percent of its appearances, and peaks modestly in paintings from the 1900s [3]. Its earliest match dates to 1150, 860 years before the name was recorded in 2010; pale warm oranges like this are common in aged varnish and skin tones alike, so the match says nothing about what any painter actually mixed, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. In printed English the phrase rose fastest in the 2000s and peaked in the 2010s [4].

origin.first_recorded: undocumented; recorded by Wikipedia and the xkcd color survey, 2010

questions.q: What is Macaroni and Cheese named after?
True or false: the xkcd color survey records only one hex value for "Macaroni and Cheese."

openers: Two different oranges share the name Macaroni and Cheese in the xkcd survey's own data.

issues: No dated source for the name's coining; said plainly as undocumented rather than guessed.
